root_cause.text: In AppArmor’s per-CPU buffer cache in `aa_get_buffer()`, an unconditional decrement of the `cache->hold` counter allowed an unsigned underflow to `UINT_MAX` when `hold` reached zero while buffers remained on the per-CPU list, preventing buffers from being returned to the global pool.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes `cache->hold--;` to `if (cache->hold) cache->hold--;` in `security/apparmor/lsm.c`, and the CVE description states that when `aa_get_buffer()` pulls from the per-cpu list it “unconditionally decrements cache->hold” and that if `hold` reaches 0 while `count` is still non-zero, “the unsigned decrement wraps to UINT_MAX,” causing `aa_put_buffer()` to stop returning buffers to the global list.

intent_record.intent_summary: Prevent cache->hold from underflowing when reusing a cached buffer in aa_get_buffer().
intent_record.what: In aa_get_buffer(), the decrement of cache->hold after removing a buffer from cache->head was wrapped in an if (cache->hold) check, so the counter is only decremented when it is nonzero. The cache->count decrement and return path remain unchanged.
intent_record.how: At runtime, this prevents cache->hold from underflowing if the function reuses a buffer when hold is already zero. The buffer allocation/retrieval behavior is otherwise unchanged, but the accounting for held buffers is now safer and avoids an invalid negative-style wraparound on the counter.

bic_trace_step.reason: The vulnerable construct described in the root cause is not present in this function body. In the shown `aa_get_buffer(bool in_atomic)`, the buffer cache is guarded by `buffer_count` and `reserve_count`: `if (buffer_count > reserve_count || (in_atomic && !list_empty(&aa_global_buffers))) { ... buffer_count--; ... }`. This avoids an unconditional decrement when the cache is empty or below reserve, which is the condition that previously allowed `cache->hold` to underflow. The corresponding put path also increments the count (`buffer_count++;`), and initialization allocates extra reserve buffers (`num = 4 + RESERVE_COUNT` / `2 + RESERVE_COUNT`). Therefore the function shown already contains the fix and does not exhibit the buggy unconditional decrement behavior.
